title: Praying for other churches
hookLine: pray for the church down the road
tomorrow: seventy days of living it. what fits on one page?
last: A WEEK OF LOVE AND THE CHURCH.

lines: WHAT DO YOU PRAY FOR IT?
cards: The church down the road: a different sign out front, different songs, maybe a different way of baptizing or of sharing the bread. People drive past it every Sunday. What do you pray for a church that isn't yours?
In Mark's Gospel, the disciples run into something like it, and they don't like it one bit.

teach.b: John reports to Jesus: “Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.” Not one of us, so we stopped him.

teach.h: NOT AGAINST US, ON OUR PART.
teach.b: Jesus answers, “Forbid him not,” and then: “For he that is not against us is on our part.” On our part. The circle is wider than the disciples drew it.

teach.h: THAT THEY ALL MAY BE ONE.
teach.b: On his last night, in John's Gospel, Jesus prays for those who will believe later: “That they all may be one.” Churches today are divided in real ways, and they read that unity differently.
Catholics, Orthodox Christians and Protestants each understand one church in their own way, and the differences are serious. Praying for another church doesn't erase them. It does something simpler.
Paul tells the church at Philippi: “I thank my God upon every remembrance of you.”

Praying for the church down the road, by name, turns a rival into a remembrance. And the whole week fits inside that prayer: love over everything, peace given, come and see, faithful honestly, hands, and support.

how: Christians pray for other churches in their own prayers and in services; some churches set aside special times of prayer for Christian unity, and neighboring congregations sometimes pray together.

games.q: what does “praying for other churches” mean?
o: trying to win members away from rival groups
asking God's help for your own congregation only
asking God's good for churches not your own

games.q: the wider circle — tap the pairs.
p: he that is not against us

s: the disciples stopped a man because he wasn't one of their group
John says: we forbad him, because he followeth not us.
Jesus told the disciples to keep stopping him
Jesus says forbid him not: he that is not against us is on our part.
Paul says love is one more virtue on the pile
he calls it the bond of perfectness, put on above all.

games.q: your cousin's youth group and yours are both running a coat drive this winter, and some kids want to turn it into a contest. what fits Mark 9?
o: team up or cheer them on: whoever isn't against us is on our part.
win the contest so everyone sees which church is right.
stop yours; two drives means one of them is in the wrong.
games.why: the disciples stopped a man because he followed not us; Jesus said forbid him not, for he that is not against us is on our part.

practice: Say the name of one church near you that isn't your own, out loud. If you pray, thank God for the people inside it and ask good things for them; if not, hold them in mind with good will.

wordCard.voice: Praying for other churches. Holding the church down the road before God, by name, with thanks, as part of one body.

orig.note: the Greek of 'that they all may be one', John 17:21.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole church. He that is not against us is on our part. Two weeks of the heart and the church, done.
